issues.description: The problem statement and NoteResource use ResponseEntity to signal HTTP response codes (e.g. returning 400 Bad Request when the client supplies an invalid person). In the solution, PersonResource.createPerson is declared to return Person and returns null on invalid input instead of returning a ResponseEntity with an appropriate status. This deviates from the expected REST handling described in the problem (and the pattern shown in NoteResource) and will not produce the intended HTTP 400 response for invalid create requests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make createPerson consistent with the pattern used in NoteResource and the problem description: change the signature to return ResponseEntity<Person> and return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build() when the provided Person has a non-null id, otherwise return ResponseEntity.ok(personService.savePerson(person)). This ensures proper HTTP status signaling for invalid input.
